- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the first 5–10 days of the forecast window, then gradually converges toward true values — suggesting lag or delayed reaction to market signals.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+ → 95+), then corrects downward — model exhibits inertia or overreaction.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to forecast lower prices than true values in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts for the first 10 days are often too low, especially when history includes recent high prices — model fails to capture momentum or volatility clustering.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the 20–30 day range, suggesting it underweights recent upward momentum or overweights long-term mean.
